scenario: S4 : async COPY offload thread-hop (svc thread -> server worker kthread -> CB_OFFLOAD callback leg -> client)
purpose: Verify remote kcov attribution continuity when the execution owner thread changes: the NFSv4.2 server async COPY is handed from the svc thread (COPY4 request) to a worker kthread (nfsd4_do_async_copy) and the completion returns to the client via a CB_OFFLOAD callback. Patch 0010 wraps the kthread in a saved-work continuation (sunrpc_fuzz_saved_work_start/stop) so its coverage still attaches to the originating remote-request flow. This corpus proves the continuation traverses the hop.

trigger_detail.client: The baked x2 workload ftruncate()s the source to 0x2000000 (32MiB) and requests 0x4000000 bytes. VFS clamps to 32MiB > 2*rsize (at most 8MiB), so nfs42_proc_copy requests async COPY and handle_async_copy waits for CB_OFFLOAD (3s initial fallback).
trigger_detail.server: nfsd4_copy saves the continuation and spawns nfsd4_do_async_copy. The saved-work section includes nfsd4_run_cb enqueue, then stops. nfsd4_run_cb_work executes later on ownerless cl_callback_wq; physical CB_OFFLOAD delivery is required separately, not attributed to the COPY generation.

fixture: tools/ab-lane-fixture-v42.sh (INLINE: prelude retires the baked boot fixture, exports NFS_MINOR_VERSION=2, then runs the baked lane.sh body verbatim in-process; a thin wrapper that forks /opt/frozen-phase9/lane.sh exhausts guest fork capacity during boot-fixture retirement -- fixture-setup rc=124/"Cannot fork"; probe evidence 2026-09-26)

attribution_model.fs/nfsd: Server code collects ONLY under ON remote kcov (off_union is empty); on_only == on_union. Sentinel membership asserted against on_only.
attribution_model.net/sunrpc: Mixed client/server; the ON-attributed slice is on_only. The saved-work continuation runs only in the server kthread, so it must land in on_only.
attribution_model.fs/nfs: Client code collects in both OFF and ON (executor plain kcov); on_only is empty by design. Sentinel presence asserted against on_union (proves the client legs executed during ON trials); OFF presence recorded for context.

ownerless_callback.correlation: Require one complete ordered event chain per execution in both modes. Match async nfs4_copy to later nfs4_cb_offload by stateid/filehandle/count within [0,3)s. Match server offload to CB_OFFLOAD queue and workqueue_queue_work on the same enqueuer task; match work identity/function to execute_start/end, and nfsd_cb_start inside that exact worker task interval before client delivery. Match later successful offload_done by client/stateid. Reject ambiguous/reversed chains, retries, missing/extra events and trace loss. A valid early callback preceding the client COPY result trace is conservatively unproven, never a PASS. Capture only after fixture setup in a workload-bracketed trace. KCOV absence is not physical absence.

verdict_criteria: PASS iff all required coverage sentinels, absent-on-only assertions, AND required physical callback witnesses pass. The callback worker must execute physically but remain absent from attributed ON-only coverage. Missing physical delivery, missing attributed continuation/enqueue, or worker coverage leakage each fails independently. This is a reach/attribution verdict, not a KCSAN-clean verdict.
notes: v1 (prog sha256 02010f0f...) FAIL root cause: VFS generic_copy_file_checks clamps count=min(0x2000000, i_size-pos); the 1MiB source shrank count to 1MiB <= 2*rsize(2MiB) => client sync=true => server took the synchronous path (nfsd4_do_copy/_nfsd_copy_file_range). Probe coverage: nfs42_proc_copy+nfsd4_copy present, async sentinels absent. Fixed in v2 by ftruncate(r2, 0x1000000): clamped count 16MiB > 2*rsize cap 8MiB => ca_synchronous=false.
kcov_request_* helpers live in kernel/kcov_request.c which has no dedicated coverage set (module partition is fs/nfs, fs/nfsd, net/sunrpc); they are code-path evidence only.

nfsd4_send_cb_offload is inlined into nfsd4_do_async_copy. nfsd4_run_cb remains REQUIRED ON-only. nfsd4_run_cb_work remains REQUIRED through nfsd_cb_start at nfs4callback.c:1857, paired with CB_OFFLOAD client acceptance/completion and server RPC completion trace events. The x2 workload uses a 32MiB source; the same two-channel contract applies.
